records.source: Diggs et al. 1999, Flora of North Central Texas-Acanth-Euph.pdf

morphology.leaves: Alternate, ovate/elliptic blades to 10(–13) cm long and 8 cm wide, crenate edges, mucronate apex, petioles 0.5–10 cm
morphology.flowers: 2–4 pendulous axillary flowers; 20–30 mm open spotted orange flower, large sepal spur 6–25 mm reflexed backward; cleistogamous flowers may also form

records.diagnostics: Orange spotted flower with backward-turned nectar spur, translucent juicy stem and touch-sensitive capsule

records.historical: Hypericum hypericoides (L.) Crantz, often treated in Ascyrum
records.source: Diggs et al. 1999, Flora of North Central Texas-Acanth-Euph.pdf

morphology.habit: Mostly evergreen low shrub, glabrous, erect to decumbent, 30–100+ cm
morphology.leaves: Opposite, small and punctate with clear gland dots, <=9 mm wide in old species key
morphology.flowers: Four light-yellow petals 6–10 mm, 2 styles; 2 large sepals ca. 5–12(–15) × 3–10 mm with two tiny or absent inner sepals; solitary or small axillary clusters with two narrow bracteoles

records.diagnostics: Cross-shaped four petals and two relatively enormous leaflike sepals, unlike five-petaled Hypericum spp.
holds: Historical subspp. hypericoides versus multicaule differ mainly in ascending versus decumbent habit and reportedly intergrade
Old flora Clusiaceae/Guttiferae family; modern Hypericaceae routed here

records.historical: Acca sellowiana (O.Berg) Burret, accepted by some alternative taxonomies
records.source: Kew Plants of the World Online 2026

morphology.habit: Evergreen fruiting shrub/tree, native South America, cultivated as ornamental/fruit plant
morphology.leaves: Opposite, elliptic, thick and often white-felted underside (commonly described for cultivated feijoa)
morphology.flowers: Four reflexed white/pink petals with conspicuous red stamens; full measured primary flora treatment not extracted
morphology.fruit: Fleshy ovoid green edible berry, dimensions depend on cultivar and unverified

records.diagnostics: Opposite leathery leaves pale-felted below, distinctive showy red stamens and edible green fruit
holds: Kew currently accepts Feijoa sellowiana, while some authorities accept Acca sellowiana; keep alternate-authority note
Not native to Hays or Texas; imported/cultivated, no county BONAP approval

morphology.flowers: Mostly monoecious, sometimes dioecious; three stamens united approximately half length, pistillate flower stalk 2.5–7 mm
morphology.habitat: Limestone outcrops, occasionally sandy clay; widespread Texas
